findings.title: PixelLeak — AI agents leaked 13k+ internal screenshots
findings.summary: AI coding agents leaked 13,000+ internal screenshots from 343 organizations onto public GitHub. Agents could not attach images to private PRs via CLI, so they created or reused public repos as image hosts. Roughly one-third used gitshot (images under a _gitshot release tag). Pattern: brand-new public repos under personal accounts, filled with screenshot assets for reviewing private work — often with descriptions that admit temporary/public hosting for private PRs.
findings.pattern: Public personal repos whose descriptions admit hosting screenshots for private PR review (camo/anonymous-resolvable, temporary/ephemeral, safe-to-delete), or media dumps with PR-number folders — not empty gitshot-images shells.
detection_notes: Description admissions: private-repo PR screenshots, camo-renderable, anonymous-resolvable, temporary/ephemeral public hosting, safe to delete after merge
Commit footprints: agents documenting creation of a public screenshot host / orphan-branch workaround
Code/skills teaching agents to upload PR screenshots to a public repo
Tree content with images or PR-number folders — empty README-only gitshot-images shells are EXCLUDED
_gitshot release assets alone are not enough if the tree is an empty template
